result.topic_en: Gauss gives a rule for computing a sign sum ε over representations of a number by a linear equation (biquadratic-residue-type counting for Gaussian integers mod 24+2i), with worked examples for 97 and 193, and a correction of −1 for numbers ≡ 3 mod (24+2i).

methods.what: Linear relation used to enumerate values for the second counting method
Sign rule: ε = +1 if [X]+Y even, −1 if odd; the sum Σε has the same meaning as before

methods.what: Correction for numbers ≡ 3 mod (24+2i): second method needs −1 added
Worked example for 193 with 14X + 24Y = 193, both methods giving 0

items.english: For numbers ≡ 3 mod (24+2i) the first method from Σ±(X+[Y]) remains valid unchanged, but to the result of the second method −1 must still be added or used.
